messages:
sanjay.k: quick heads-up — noticed a ~12% p99 latency bump when running the replay harness for JSON-mode function calls vs the synthetic load. numbers below. anyone else see this?

maria: hmm, is that with the same kernel selection profile? or did the harness trigger different kernels because of token shapes?

sanjay.k: same model and quant, same sequence length distribution (we pinned to 128/256 mixed). profiler shows more small-kernel matmuls during structured output validation.

liam: can you paste the flamegraph? even a short snippet helps.

sanjay.k: pasted minimal trace:
```
TRACE: serve.core -> kernel_selector -> pick: small_gemm_16x128 (80%)
TRACE: batching -> dynamic_merge: avg_batch=4.2 -> more per-request overhead
TRACE: kvcache -> hit_rate=0.72, misses spike during nested func calls
TRACE: json_validator -> parse+schema-check add ~1.8ms/op
```

maria: interesting — small_gemm shows up more in replay because the replay harness splits long tool args into separate messages, so we end up with many short seq calls. synthetic traffic concatenated prompts into one long request.

jen: that implies batching heuristics are different: replay fosters many small batches, synthetic more steady medium batches. we should control for that. proposal: run synthetic runner but replay the exact sequence boundaries (no concat).

liam: also check KV cache warmup. Replay may invalidate prefix patterns causing misses. if kv miss increases we get extra kernel warmups and <50% throughput.

perf-bot: loadtest scheduled: run-id=run-2026-03-18-01, config: replay-seq-boundaries=true, kvcache-mode=enabled, kernel-hint=none

sanjay.k: results from run-id above (aggregates):
- throughput: replay-as-is 620 req/s -> replay-boundaries 410 req/s
- p50/p95/p99: 12/48/180 ms -> 14/52/200 ms (so slight latency up but more stable)
- kvcache hit: 0.72 -> 0.89 after adjusting boundary preservation
- json validation failures: 0.6% -> 0.6% (unchanged)

maria: weird that kvcache went up but latency got a bit worse. could be batching: avg batch size down from 6.5 -> 3.1 so higher per-token overhead.

liam: check kernel selection plot: when batch size drops, kernel_selector chooses small_gemm_16x128 for most steps (fast for tiny batches) but more kernel-switch overhead (context switch + jit lookup) adds latency. we should measure kernel switch cost.

jen: what about validation cost? json validator is sync right now, if it runs in main thread it serializes work. consider async validation off critical path and speculative accept then post-validate + retry on fail.

sanjay.k: ran an experiment: async-validate=true, optimistic-accept=true, retry-on-fail=true. Observed: p99 improved 12% vs baseline, but error-retries increased application-level retries by 0.9% leading to a 1.6% increase in overall token usage.

maria: cost tradeoff: lower latency at the expense of more tokens. need a policy: for live customers prefer lower latency with retry cap; for batch offline prefer stricter validation.

liam: also spotted a perf regression in the kernel selector after the last micro-optim: lookup cache invalidation frequency doubled in the replay scenario. looks like we evict per-request hints when request metadata size > 256 bytes. the replay harness attaches metadata for trace correlation, which pushed us over the threshold.

jen: easy fix: stash only hash of metadata for hint key. will open PR to avoid invalidating hint cache.

perf-bot: regression ticket created: INF-9842 (kernel-selector hint eviction)

sanjay.k: next steps I propose: 1) run controlled synthetic with exact replay boundaries (we did that), 2) run same with metadata-hash patch, 3) test async validation tradeoffs with retry caps, 4) measure kernel-switch overhead microbenchmark.

maria: agree. I'll schedule runs and add a short checklist to the bench harness so we can reproduce apples-to-apples: sequence boundaries, metadata size, kvcache warmup, and validation mode.

liam: for the kernel-switch microbench I can craft a synthetic that flips candidates every few steps to emulate the replay jitter — will post results.

jen: PR: github.com/redwood/infer/PR/4021 — kernel-hint stash hash. measuring locally shows hint eviction rate down 70% on replay traces.

sanjay.k: perfect. once PR lands we'll re-run run-id=run-2026-03-18-01 and report numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: job update: run-id=run-2026-03-18-01 requeued after PR merge.

maria: logging outcome here when finished, keeping this thread for a concise audit of the investigation.
